title: Getting A Medical Card | CastleLeaf
description: How the Massachusetts medical marijuana program works in general terms: certifying providers, registering with the Commission and caregivers. Adult-use note.
lede: A plain-language look at how the Massachusetts medical marijuana program works. One thing first: CastleLeaf is an adult-use only store, so we don't serve the medical program.

blocks.html: CastleLeaf is an Adult-Use only retail provider. We don't serve the state's medical program, and a medical card isn't what gets you in our door: to shop with us, all you need is a valid government ID that shows you're 21+.
Massachusetts voters approved medical marijuana in 2012, and today the program is overseen by the Cannabis Control Commission. In broad strokes, it runs like this.

items.title: See a certifying provider
items.text: A healthcare provider who is registered with the program as a certifying provider decides whether to issue you a certification.

items.title: Register with the Commission
items.text: With a certification in place, you register as a patient with the Cannabis Control Commission, following the steps it publishes.

items.title: Shop at a medical dispensary
items.text: Registered patients buy from dispensaries licensed to serve the medical program, under that program's own rules.

blocks.html: The program also recognizes caregivers: adults who register with the program so they can purchase on a registered patient's behalf.
Eligibility, fees and processing times are set by the program and can change, so the most reliable source is the Cannabis Control Commission itself.
And if you're 21 or older and simply curious about cannabis, you're welcome at CastleLeaf as an adult-use shopper. Our dispensary guide walks you through a first visit.
This page is a plain-language summary, not legal or medical advice.
